study type: Retrospective observational study with intervention comparison
exposure: Interventions to reduce CS rates (free mobilization of pregnant women, CS decision with signature of three obstetricians, re-evaluation of CS decision, strictly obeying failed induction algorithm)
cohort: The study included 100,326 deliveries at Zekai Tahir Burak Research and Training Hospital in Ankara, Turkey, between 2012 and 2018.
finding: The overall cesarean section rate significantly reduced from 44.7% (2012-2017) to 42.0% (2017) after the implementation of specific interventions.
mod_finding: The implemented interventions resulted in a significant reduction in overall cesarean section rates, indicating an impact on the mode of birth.
